# The names

Where neon1, its slogan and its products get their names.

## neon1

The name nods to Neo from *The Matrix*, who brought peace between man and machine. Neo means new, and neon is unmissable. It's always written with a lowercase n.

## "1 is glad to be of service."

The slogan nods to Robin Williams' Andrew from *Bicentennial Man*, a machine who spends two centuries being of service while searching for his humanity. The 1 is me, Pradeep, neon1's sole owner.

## The legal names

- **neon1 LLC**, a New York limited liability company, does business as **neon1**, a registered assumed name (see the [state registration](registration.md)).
- **N1 Supply LLC** does business as **N1 Supply**. It is an affiliate of neon1 LLC.

## Product names

Repositories that neon1 builds mainly for its own use carry the `neon1-` prefix, such as neon1-site and neon1-corpus. Products made for the public or for clients get names of their own, such as [Ready, Secure, Go](../products/ready-secure-go.md).

# Contact

How to reach neon1, when, and what the first call covers.

| | |

| **GitHub** | [neon1llc](https://github.com/neon1llc) |

## What to expect

- **Where:** remote across the US, or on site within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. Outside the US, ask.
- **When:** Monday to Thursday 6pm to 9pm, Friday 6pm to 8pm, and weekends 8am to 8pm, Eastern time.
- **Size:** a week or two up to about six weeks for one piece of work. Larger efforts split into phases, each with its own scope, price, and handover, approved before it starts. A few clients at a time.
- **First call:** free, 30 minutes, about your needs. Options come afterward, in writing. [What to bring](../guides/first-call.md).
- **Before the call, if you like:** outline up to three projects in a [1NEON account](../guides/free-accounts.md) and ask for an assessment. I read them before we talk. Neither needs the other first.
- **After:** a short proposal. Nothing starts until you approve it.

## Availability and urgent issues

I work in planned appointments on weekday evenings and weekends, with no 24/7 or emergency response. If something can't wait, such as a security incident in progress, an outage, or fraud on an account, contact a provider with emergency coverage, and your bank or the service involved, first. Ongoing care after a project, with any response times, is agreed in writing before it starts.

## Report a bug

Something broken on neon1.tech, 1NEON, or Neo? [Report a bug](https://neon1.tech/report-bug/) with where and what happened, plus an optional email and screenshots.

Leave passwords, health details, and payment information out of any message or report.

# How a project runs

Listen, propose, decide, build, and hand over.

1. **Listen.** The goal, the systems and people involved, the constraints, and who will own the result. It starts with a 30-minute call, and I read anything you've written in a 1NEON account first.
2. **Propose.** A recommendation, or options when there's a real choice, each with scope, acceptance criteria, cost to build and run, and alternatives considered.
3. **Decide.** You approve the scope and price. Sometimes the answer is a setting, an existing product, or leaving things as they are.
4. **Build.** Reviewable changes, tested against the acceptance criteria, including failure and rollback. Scope changes need your approval.
5. **Hand over.** Evidence that it meets the criteria, documentation, and a walkthrough for whoever runs it. Ongoing care is optional.

[Walk through a fictional project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live) in 1NEON.

# Service agreement

neon1's service agreement, as a client organization signs it once in 1NEON: how work is agreed, purchases, paying and disputes, review and acceptance, delays, defects, ownership, confidentiality, case studies, records, limits, ending, and law.

**The short version**

- One agreement covers every project, and each option you approve sets its scope, price, and timeline.
- Invoices are due in 15 days, and paying never depends on, or counts as, accepting the work.
- You review and accept the work yourself; silence never counts, and you choose about case studies.

Edition 2.4

This agreement is between neon1 LLC, doing business as neon1 ("neon1", "I", "me"), 418 Broadway, Ste R, Albany, NY 12207, and the organization named where it is signed in 1NEON ("you"), at the legal name and mailing address recorded with the signature. It covers every project I do for you while it is in effect.

## How work is agreed

Each project has a proposal in 1NEON, issued in numbered revisions. A proposal lists the services, what each is worth, the rate or price, the billing schedule, and the result you'll be able to check. When your decision maker approves an option, its ID (for example 0039-r2-B) fixes that project's scope, price, and timeline. A change is agreed the same way, by approving an option in the next revision. This agreement governs everything else. If a proposal and this agreement disagree, this agreement wins, unless the proposal names the section it changes.

## Purchases

Prices for equipment, software, and services from other vendors are estimates. You buy them yourself, in your name, unless an approval says that I buy them for you. When I do, you pay me back exactly what I paid, shown by the receipt in 1NEON, with no markup.

## Paying

I invoice through 1NEON for work performed under an approved proposal, according to its billing schedule. For estimated work, I bill the hours worked at the agreed rate, every two weeks unless the proposal says otherwise. Each hour is listed in 1NEON, and the total never passes the estimate's high end unless you approve a change first. For a fixed price, set for a small, well-defined job, I bill by the agreed milestones or on delivery, and that price is the whole price for the work described. Unforeseen work or purchases are agreed with you before I add them. I send each invoice within 7 days after the period, milestone, or delivery it bills.

An option may ask for a deposit when it is approved: 30% of a fixed price or of an estimate's low end, unless the proposal states another share. A deposit counts toward later invoices. If the work done comes to less than a deposit you paid, I refund the difference.

Each invoice is due within 15 days unless we agree otherwise in writing. Payment for properly performed work does not depend on you recording acceptance, and paying an invoice does not mean you have accepted the work or given up a valid claim. You can pay by bank transfer (ACH), card, check, Zelle, or wire.

If you believe an invoice includes work that was not agreed, performed, or delivered as required, tell me in 1NEON which part you dispute and why, and we will work to resolve it. The undisputed amount stays payable by its original due date.

I send a reminder the business day after an invoice is due. If an undisputed amount is more than 7 days overdue, I may pause work until it is paid, after telling you in writing.

## Review and acceptance

When the work is ready, I hand it over: the agreed deliverables, the documentation, and the access you need to use and review the work. I record that date in 1NEON and tell you in writing. Please review the work within 10 business days, and record your acceptance in 1NEON or tell me what does not work as agreed.

If an agreed check fails, I correct the work and present it again for review. Silence never counts as acceptance. A delay in your review does not postpone payment for properly performed work or change the agreed payment schedule.

## When I'm waiting on you

You give me timely answers, the access the work needs, and accounts held in your organization's name. Please don't put passwords or other secrets in 1NEON.

If I cannot continue because I am waiting for your access, information, decisions, or participation, I tell you what is needed and how the delay affects the work. If the delay continues for 10 business days after that notice, I may pause the affected work and adjust its schedule. If it continues for 30 calendar days, I may end the affected project as described under Ending.

You remain responsible for work properly performed and purchases you approved before a pause or ending. I don't charge for work not yet done merely because a project is delayed.

## Quality and defect correction

I do the work with care. I fix defects in the agreed work at no charge when you report them within 30 days of handover. A defect is something that does not work as the proposal requires. Handover happens only when I have actually provided what the work needs, as described under Review and acceptance; marking a project complete doesn't start the 30 days on its own. Defects reported in that time remain mine to fix until they are resolved. This period does not limit rights or remedies that the law doesn't allow to be limited.

## Ownership

Once you have paid for a project, what I made for you in it is yours: configurations, scripts, documents, and training material. Until then, you may use it in your business as the work intends. I keep my general know-how and the tools I had before or build for my own use. Where your work uses one of those tools, you get a permanent license to use it in your business. Open-source and third-party software stays under its own license.

Your existing systems, data, accounts, credentials, and business records are always yours. Whatever is owed, I never disable your systems, withhold your credentials or data, or delete anything of yours.

## Confidentiality

We each keep what we learn about the other's business private, and use it only for the work. This doesn't cover what is already public, what the law requires us to disclose, or what your choices below allow.

## Case studies

You can choose whether I may describe our work publicly in anonymized case studies, articles, or examples. Your choice does not affect the services I provide or their price.

Anonymized means that neither the information itself nor its combination with other reasonably available information can reasonably identify your organization, your people, or your customers. I never publish your confidential information, personal information, security-sensitive details, or identifiable records.

You choose when you sign. Nothing is selected for you:

- **Yes.** Anonymized case studies are fine.
- **Decide later.** I ask you about each project before publication.
- **No.** I don't publish case studies about your projects.

## Your name and identifying material

You also choose whether I may list your organization's name as a client: **ask me first**, **yes**, or **no**.

Your name, logo or trademarks, quotations or testimonials, endorsements, identifiable screenshots, and linking your name to a particular case study each take a separate yes. Permission for anonymized case studies does not cover them.

An admin can change these choices in 1NEON at any time, and the change applies from then on. If you withdraw permission, I stop further use and remove the affected material from the places I control. I can't guarantee removal of independent copies or archives kept by others.

## Regulated data

I don't handle health records, payment card data, or similar regulated personal data unless we sign a separate agreement for it first, such as a business associate agreement.

## Records

1NEON keeps a record of notices, handovers, review requests, acceptances, invoices, disputes, reminders, pauses, and endings, and either of us can rely on it. I keep signed agreements, approvals, invoices, and payment records for seven years as my business practice, and longer when an actual or reasonably expected dispute, investigation, or legal obligation needs them. If you ask me to delete something, I will, except what I must keep for those reasons.

## Limits

Neither of us is liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses, such as lost profits. My total liability for all claims about a project is limited to the fees paid and payable for that project. These limits don't apply to gross negligence, willful misconduct, a breach of confidentiality, or anything the law doesn't allow to be limited, and they never reduce what you owe for work properly performed and purchases you approved.

## Ending

Either of us may end this agreement, or one project under it, with 14 days' written notice, by message in 1NEON or by email. Ending a project for a delay, as described above, also takes written notice.

When it ends, you pay for work properly performed and purchases you approved up to that point, not the price of work not yet done, and I refund any unearned deposit. I return your access and credentials and hand over the work made so far, with its records, which becomes yours once it is paid for. Ownership, confidentiality, your choices about case studies and your name, records, limits, and payment owed continue after it ends.

## Disputes and law

We will first try to settle any disagreement by talking it through. New York law governs this agreement, and disputes go to the state or federal courts in New York County, New York. Nothing in this agreement waives rights the law doesn't allow to be waived.

## Signing

I work as an independent contractor, not an employee. This agreement and the approved proposals under it are our whole agreement, and it changes only by a new edition signed in 1NEON.

We agree to sign and keep these records electronically. The person signing confirms that they are authorized to sign for your organization, and their typed name in 1NEON is a signature. 1NEON keeps the exact text signed, its edition, the time, and who signed, and you can download a copy or ask me for a paper one at any time.

# How 1NEON accounts work

Start before we talk: make a 1NEON account, outline up to three projects, then ask for an assessment. The 30-minute call is the other way in.

[1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/) is the portal my clients use. You can start in it before we talk: outline your project, then ask for an assessment of up to three projects, or book the first call. I read what you wrote first. No card, no password.

[Create an account](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/?signup=1)

## How it goes

1. **Sign up** with your email, your name, which describes you best, and your organization's name if you have one. A website or location is optional. A code emailed to you finishes it.
2. **Outline a project.** **Next step** on Home and the project's **Overview** show six optional parts to write, with a tip for each missing one. [What to write](#what-to-write) shows what a good answer looks like.
3. **Ask for an assessment** from **Next step**: choose one to three projects and add a required note of a sentence or two. I reply by email with a likely approach and the first questions to settle. It isn't a design, a proposal, or the paid [assessment](../engagement/index.md) with costed next steps. It goes to me 30 minutes after your last change, so you can edit or withdraw it until then.
4. **We talk,** if you like. Message me any time in the chat (the round Neo button, then **neon1**), or talk for 30 minutes: book from **Next step**, ask me to email you, or use **Contact neon1** in the menu. Options come afterward, in writing.
5. **If it fits,** we agree on the work and your account becomes a client account. Everything you wrote stays, and the outline becomes the plan.

I work remotely across the US, and on site within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. Outside the US, ask.

## What to write

An outline is what you write down about a project before I assess it. Every part is optional, and a short answer is enough. A part counts when it holds real words, about a dozen characters or more, and an unanswered starter question doesn't count. A project is outlined with the first three parts and fully outlined with all six.

| Part | Write | Where it goes once the work starts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **What it is** | The project in a sentence or two: the summary on the Overview. | The scope in the proposal. |
| **How it works today** | One real example of how it works today, answered in Needs. | The starting point Observe measures against. |
| **What done looks like** | What will be true when it's done: the outcome on the Overview. | The checks in Verify that say it's finished. |
| **Who and what it touches** | Who does this work and the tools it touches: an answered question or a system added in Needs. | The handover in Normalize: accounts, access, and training. |
| **How we'll know it worked** | A measure with where it is now, added in Observe. | Tracked in Observe, before and after. |
| **Timing and limits** | A target date, or limits such as budget or must-nots. | The proposal's schedule and constraints. |

### What a good answer looks like

These are made up, for a building-supply yard.

- **What it is:** "Turn phone and email quote requests into one queue, so none are missed."
- **How it works today:** "On Tuesday a contractor's email for 40 sheets of drywall sat unseen for three days."
- **What done looks like:** "Every request gets a quote within one business day."
- **Who and what it touches:** "Two counter staff and the owner. Email, the phone line, and the inventory spreadsheet."
- **How we'll know it worked:** "Quote time, now about 2 days."
- **Timing and limits:** "Before the spring rush, with nothing that changes the till."

## What it holds

| | Free account | Client account |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Projects | 3 | No set limit |
| Needs and notes in a project | 50 | No set limit |
| Files | 10 files, 10 MB each, 50 MB total | Up to 100 MB each |
| Inviting your team, proposals, approvals, and invoices | Once we work together | Yes |
| Message me in the chat | Yes | Yes |
| Who sees it | You and me | Your team and me |

## How long it lasts

Home shows the date your account is kept until. If nothing changes, you get reminders at 7 and 14 days, a final notice at 21, and at 30 days the account and what's in it are deleted. **Keep it 30 more days** on Home (once) if you need more time, and **Download a copy** any time. While an outline is unfinished and nothing is waiting for me, you also get outline tips by email about 3 and 7 days after your last change. Turn them off under Outline tips in your profile's Notifications.

Section 3 of the [terms of use](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/terms) covers these accounts, and the [privacy and data policy](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/privacy) covers what sign-up collects, including Cloudflare's invisible check that you're a person. I don't add you to a mailing list.

# 1NEON help

Short answers about using the 1NEON client portal.

Signed in? Tap **?** at the top right of any page for help with that page.

## Getting started

### What is 1NEON?
The portal where we run your projects together: what you need, the work, the results, and the handover. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### Can I try it first?
Yes, without signing in. The [guided walkthrough](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live) plays a made-up project on the real portal in about three minutes, and the full story takes about 20 minutes. The [sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) is a made-up project to read. The [interactive demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/) is a working copy where you pick who to be, and changes stay in your browser until **Start over**. [From sign-up to client](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=free) follows one account from sign-up to client. Short walkthroughs show one thing: [joining from an invitation](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite), [adding a passkey](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey), [adding an authenticator app](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator), and [texts and text codes](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### How do I get in?
When sign-up is open, choose **Create an account** on the sign-in screen. Otherwise, open the link in an invite email. Sign in with a code sent to your email, or with a passkey. There's no password. Watch [creating an account](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=free) or [joining from an invite](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### I didn't get the sign-in code.
Check spam or promotions, wait a minute, then choose **Send a new code**. A code works for a few minutes, in the browser that asked. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### Is there a tour?
Yes, at your first sign-in. Replay it from **?** or your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### What do I do first in a new account?
Outline up to three projects, then ask for an assessment under **Next step** on Home. **Get to know 1NEON** links to a sample project, a walkthrough, the demo, and these FAQs. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=free).

### What is an outline?
What you write about a project before I assess it, in six parts: what it is, how it works today, what done looks like, who and what it touches, a measure, and timing and limits. Every part is optional, and a short answer is enough. **Next step** on Home and the project's **Overview** show what's written, with a tip for each missing part. [What to write](https://neon1.tech/knowledge/guides/free-accounts/#what-to-write) has examples.

### What is Ready for Execute?
The percent on a project's **Overview**, before the work starts. Each outline part is 10, the assessment 10, options 10, and an approved option 20, so 100% needs a decision. Then the outline carries into the work: its measure is tracked in **Observe**, its people and tools shape the handover in **Normalize**, and what done looks like becomes the checks in Verify. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=free).

### How do I ask for an assessment?
Under **Next step** on Home, write the note (required, a sentence or two), choose one to three projects, and choose **Request assessment**, then **Submit request**. It goes to me 30 minutes after your last change, so you can **Edit** or **Withdraw** it until then. An edit after that goes out as an update. I reply by email.

### Do I need a call first?
No. The assessment and the call are separate ways in. **Next step** has **Book a 30-minute call**, or **ask me to email you** (once a week).

### Will I get emails about my outline?
In a new account, yes: while an outline is unfinished and nothing is waiting for me, tips arrive about 3 and 7 days after your last change, then no more. Turn them off under **Outline tips** in your profile's **Notifications**. Clients don't get them unless they turn them on.

### How do I hide or bring back Get to know 1NEON?
Choose **Hide** on the card. To bring it back, open your profile and choose **Show Get to know 1NEON on Home** under Tutorial.

## Projects and the four layers

### What are Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize?
The four layers of every project. **Needs** is what you want and the options, **Execute** the work, **Observe** the results against the goals, and **Normalize** the handover, training, and care. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### What should I do first on a project?
Read **Next step** at the top. It says what has to happen now and who it's waiting on. On a new project, **Ready for Execute** says what to write next. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### What do Not assessed, On track, At risk, and Off track mean?
They're the project's health, as the team sets it. A new project is **Not assessed** until then, and moving stages doesn't change it. Items have their own status: To do, In progress, Blocked, or Done. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we rename, reorder, or hide stages?
Projects follow the new names and order. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it. Decide still asks for an approved option, and Closed still ends a project.

### How do I tell you what I need?
On the **Needs** tab, tap **Add request** and finish a sentence with a few taps. Only the first choice is required. **Define another need** adds more. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=needs).

### Do I have to write a lot?
No. Each section shows an example and one-tap suggestions, and a short answer is enough. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### How do I know when something changes?
The bell glows. Tap it to see what changed and who changed it. Important changes also email you, and you choose which under **Notifications** in your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### How do I comment or change an item?
Tap its title to open its status, owner, due date, details, and comments, which your whole organization sees. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### How do I check something off?
Tick the box beside it. A choice between options counts once one is approved, and a measure at its target. Status updates, decisions, and uploaded files don't count, but a **File needed** does, ticked when you send it. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

### How do I delete something?
Use the trash button or **Delete** in its panel, and confirm. Approved options and decisions can't be deleted, since they record what was agreed. Files can be deleted by their uploader and admins.

### What does the onion next to a project mean?
Progress. Needs is the center ring and Normalize the outside, each filling as work gets done.

### What does the board show?
Every project as a card in its stage. Hold a card to move it, or use its **Move to** menu. Move a closed project back the same way, or choose **Reopen**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What does the timeline show?
Under **Projects**, **Timeline** draws each project from start to target date, colored by layer. The dashed line is today, the diamond the target, and red stripes time past the target. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=care).

### How do I start a project?
Choose **New project** and answer a few questions. It starts with a checklist you can change later. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### Is there a simpler way for a small job?
Yes. For a fix of a few hours, I start a **Quick fix** with no proposal. I send one quote: an estimate capped at the most hours quoted, or a fixed price when the job is small and well defined. Nothing is paid up front. **Next step** says **Approve the quote**, and you sign once. When it's fixed, you accept that one step with your signature, and I send one invoice. Your organization still signs the service agreement once before its first approval.

### What is the calendar on Home?
Due dates, milestones, project targets, and your organization's events, a month at a time. Choose a day to see them. Editors add leave, closures, meetings, or care plan dates, one-off or repeating. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=calendar).

### Where are the charts?
On Home, under Visuals in View: finished per week, project health, and delivery (open and overdue work, on-time finishes, days to a decision, measures at target), beside projects at a glance and by layer. Hover a number for how it's counted. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=observe).

## Proposals, decisions, and signing

### What is a proposal revision?
My options are issued together as a numbered proposal, such as 0039-r1, each option with its own ID, such as 0039-r1-B. Issuing freezes a copy, so what you approve is what you read. Changed options come in the next revision (0039-r2), and earlier ones stay readable, marked as replaced. Past a revision's price recheck date, approval waits for a refresh. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### How do I approve an option?
On **Needs**, compare the options and choose **Approve this option**. Add any conditions, type your full name, and tick the box. Your typed name is your signature. The approval records the option's terms as shown (ID, description, price and whether it's fixed or an estimate, hours, rate, timeline, outside costs, and purchases) with your name and the time. To ask for a change, comment on the option or send a marked-up proposal. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I download the proposal?
Yes. **Read the proposal**, under the options, puts everything on one page. **Print or save as PDF** keeps a copy, and **Download Word** gives one to mark up. Each page carries the number, such as 0039-r1. Approving in 1NEON counts the same as signing on paper. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### How do I suggest changes to a proposal?
Comment on an option, or mark up the Word download and upload it to **Files**. When 1NEON asks "Is this a revision of Proposal 0039-r1?", choose **Yes**. neon1 answers with the next revision. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Who buys equipment or software for a project?
You do, in your organization's name, unless you agree neon1 does. Expected purchases appear under **Purchases** in Execute once you approve. Mark each bought and **Attach the receipt**. neon1 buys only with the decision maker's signature or initials, and is paid back at cost, with the receipt. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we need something new after approving?
Add it as a request. If it changes the agreed scope, it waits for the next revision with its own price, so no work or cost is added without a written change.

### Who can approve?
The project's named decision maker, or, if none, an admin of your organization. Only an admin can name or change the decision maker, under **People** on the overview. Each change is recorded. neon1 can't be named, except in its own organization. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I change my mind after approving an option?
Yes, until you accept the handover. The decision maker uses **Choose this instead** on another option, says why, and signs again. Nothing is billed twice: what was invoiced for the earlier option counts toward the new one, hours already worked count toward its hours, and any overpayment comes back as a credit at handover. The earlier decision stays on record, marked replaced, with your reason on the new one. To return to a replaced option, I confirm it in the next revision with today's prices. If no option fits the change, ask me for a new one. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### What does approving an option commit us to?
That your organization agreed to the option as shown: its scope, cost, timeline, and conditions. Both sides can rely on it, alongside your signed agreement with neon1, which governs the paid work.

### How do I accept a handover step?
On **Normalize**, steps are ticked as they're done. Once all are, the decision maker chooses **Accept the handover** and signs with their typed name. One signature accepts every step. **Check it and accept** accepts one step early. Accepted steps can't be edited, and acceptance prompts the final invoice. Watch [the handover](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover) and [the final invoice](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=final). Work is accepted only when someone records it. While a decision waits on you, email reminds you after 3 and 7 business days.

### What do Cost, Quality, and Effort mean?
neon1's 1 to 5 rating of each option, where more dots is always better. **Cost** is the total cost, **Quality** how fully it meets your requirements, and **Effort** your team's effort to adopt and run it. **How this adds up** shows the hours and when you'd pay. Demo and walkthrough figures are illustrative. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

## Files

### How do I send a file?
Use **Upload** next to a file I asked for, or upload in **Files**. Files filed at **Organization level** belong to your whole organization. Choose a project to file under it, in one of its layers or at **Project level** for the project as a whole. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### Can I move a file later?
Yes. Choose **Move** on a file and pick Organization level, a project, or a layer. Only where it's listed changes.

### Are files safe?
Every file is virus-checked before anyone can download it and stays private to your organization.

### What can I upload?
A free account holds up to 10 files, 10 MB each and 50 MB in all. A client account takes any file up to 100 MB. What not to upload is in the [terms of use](../policies/terms.md).

## People and access

### What can viewers, editors, and admins do?
Viewers read and comment. Editors also add and change work. Admins also invite people and change access and settings. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### How do I invite someone?
Admins choose **Invite people** on **People**, and the person gets an email link. If it didn't go out or got lost, choose **Resend**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### Can 1NEON text me?
Once texts are on. Add your mobile number on your profile, agree to texts, save, and type the code 1NEON texts you. Texts say only that something new is waiting, with a link, and never name your organization, projects, or files. Reply STOP to turn them off. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### Why does it ask me to confirm it's me?
Admin actions (inviting people, changing access or settings, and deleting a project or someone else's comment or file) also need a recent confirmation with a passkey, an authenticator app, or a text-message code. That way a stolen email account isn't enough. Add one under Two-step verification on your profile, and a second is a backup. You won't be asked again for 12 hours in that sign-in. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

### Can I use an authenticator app?
Yes. On your profile, choose **Set up** next to Authenticator app, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type the 6-digit code. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator).

### What's a passkey?
A sign-in with your face, fingerprint, or device PIN instead of a code. It's phishing-resistant, since it only works on the real 1NEON site. Add one under Two-step verification on your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

## Your account

### How do I change my name or the look?
Open your profile from the menu to change your name, title, time zone, menu, or notifications. Most changes save by themselves. The theme and dark mode switches are at the bottom of the menu. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=profile).

### How do I sign out?
Open the menu, tap the sign-out icon beside your name, then tap **Sign out**. Or choose **Sign out** on your profile.

### I lost my phone or my authenticator app.
You can still sign in with an emailed code. The second step is only for admin actions. If you have another method, confirm with it, then remove the lost one and add a new one. If you've lost every method, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) from your account's address. Email alone isn't enough, since a stolen mailbox is what the second step guards against, so I confirm who you are by calling a number already on record (never one from the email), plus another admin's written OK if your organization has one. Then I remove the lost methods, record it, and email you. Only admin actions wait meanwhile. There's no self-service reset.

### My email address changed.
Your email is how 1NEON knows you, so you can't change it on your profile. Ask an admin to invite the new address and deactivate the old one, or email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech). Earlier work stays under the old address.

### Who do I ask for access?
An admin of your organization. If you don't know who that is, or neon1's access needs to change, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

## Invoices and paying

### Is a price fixed or an estimate?
Usually an estimate, and the option says which. **How this adds up** shows the work behind it. An estimate is a range of hours at the option's hourly rate, set after discovery. You pay for hours worked, each listed as logged, never past the high end without your approval. Unforeseen work or purchases are agreed before I add them. A small, well-defined job may carry a fixed price instead: the whole price for the work described, changed only by a change you approve. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Where do I see the hours worked?
In **Hours**, under Execute. Each entry has its date, what it went to, and its length in quarter hours. Billed hours carry the invoice's number. On a fixed price, hours are a record, not a bill. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if the work needs more hours than the estimate?
The high end is the most you pay for the approved work. Hours past it are listed, not billed. If the work itself must change, neon1 says so before the high end and issues a revision with the new price, and nothing is added until you approve. If the work takes less than the deposit covered, neon1 refunds the difference as a credit.

### Where are invoices and payments?
In **Invoices**, under Execute, with what's paid and left on each. Each opens on neon1's letterhead with its number, lines, due date, and how to pay, ready to print or save as a PDF. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### How do I pay an invoice?
Choose **Pay**. Stripe's hosted page opens for bank transfer (ACH, preferred) or card, and 1NEON never sees your details. A card shows as paid within a minute. A bank transfer shows as started that day and paid once it clears, usually in a few business days. Check, Zelle, or wire work too, with the invoice number in the memo, and neon1 records them on arrival. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### What if my bank payment doesn't go through?
No money moved. The invoice reopens with the failed payment listed, and 1NEON tells you and neon1 that day. Choose **Pay again** or another way to pay. Nothing is added to what you owe.

### Do I get a receipt?
The invoice is your receipt. Once paid it reads **Paid in full**, with each payment's date, amount, and method, and prints or saves as a PDF. Billing contacts are also emailed when a payment arrives.

### Is there a fee for paying by card, or for paying late?
No. The total is what you pay, however you pay, with no card surcharge, late fee, or interest. A late invoice shows as overdue, you get a reminder the business day after it's due, and neon1 may pause work, after telling you, once an undisputed amount is more than 7 days overdue.

### What if I think an invoice is wrong?
Open it and choose **Dispute part of this invoice**, with the amount and why. neon1 answers on the invoice and fixes a real mistake with a credit, or voids it with a reason and issues a new one, on the record. The undisputed amount stays due on the original date.

### When are invoices sent?
As your option's **When you pay** says. A deposit, 30% of a fixed price or of an estimate's low end unless the option says otherwise, comes at approval. On an estimate, the hours worked are billed every two weeks; a fixed price by its milestones or on delivery. The final invoice comes at handover, whether or not your review is finished. Purchases are billed at cost with the receipt, and care plans monthly. Invoices are due in 15 days unless the option says otherwise, and each emails your billing contacts. Watch [the deposit](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay) and [the final invoice](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=final).

### Can an invoice be changed?
Not once issued. A mistake is fixed with a credit, or by voiding it with a reason, both on record. An invoice with a payment, or one clearing, can't be voided.

### What is the service agreement?
neon1's terms for all work with your organization: how work is agreed, paying, ownership, confidentiality, and ending it. An admin signs it once in 1NEON, from **Settings**, before the first approval. Read it any time at [/1NEON/agreement](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/agreement). [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

## Support and your data

### Something urgent is wrong. Who do I tell?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) with what happened and when. neon1 works planned hours with no emergency response, so for something that can't wait, such as bank fraud or an outage, contact the provider responsible first. Report a security problem in the portal itself to [security@neon1.tech](mailto:security@neon1.tech).

### Can we get a copy of our data?
Yes, any time, without asking me. An admin opens **Settings** and chooses **Download everything** under Your data. The zip holds every project's records, decisions and signatures, proposals, invoices, payments, and handover steps as JSON and CSV, plus every comment, the activity history, every uploaded file as uploaded, and projects in Trash. README.txt says what each file holds, and manifest.json lists every file with a SHA-256 checksum. Not included: unissued invoice drafts, files still uploading, and each person's notifications, sign-in methods, and display preferences. If anything is missing, the file ends in -partial.zip instead of -complete.zip, and the README and Settings say what and why.

### What happens to our data when the work ends?
It's kept as the record of our work unless your organization asks me to delete it. Your organization can stop using 1NEON any time and download everything from Settings first. The [privacy policy](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/privacy) has the details, including how long backups and audit records last.

### Can I message you directly?
Yes. Open the round Neo button at the bottom of any page and choose **neon1**. Everyone in your organization sees the conversation, with names, and **private** keeps one message between you and me. You can edit your own messages, and a reply also comes to your email. I pause chat for anyone who spams or abuses it.

### Who can I contact?
Message me in the chat, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech), or see [Contact](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/contact).

# Working with neon1

Short answers on where, when, how long, cost, and how data is handled.

## Do you come on site?

Yes, within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. Otherwise I work remotely across the US, or on your network through a connection I remove when the job's done. Outside the US, ask.

## When do you work?

Monday to Thursday 6pm to 9pm, Friday 6pm to 8pm, and weekends 8am to 8pm, Eastern, for about 10 to 20 project hours a week. Meetings with your team fit those windows. I plan any change to a live system, like a cutover, with your team ahead of time and keep a rollback ready. When a step waits on a vendor or your staff during the day, I work from the written plan and pick up as soon as it clears. The booking calendar shows what's open.

## Can I start without a call?

Yes. [Start a 1NEON account](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/?signup=1), outline up to three projects on your own time, then ask for an assessment of any or all of them. I read them and reply by email, and you can message me in the chat from your account.

Neither the call nor the assessment needs the other first. [Book a call](https://calendly.com/book-neon1/initial) whenever you'd rather talk. [How 1NEON accounts work](https://neon1.tech/knowledge/guides/free-accounts/) has the details.

## How do you treat our data and accounts?

I use only the access the job needs, keep your information confidential, and remove my access when we're done. We sign a short [service agreement](../engagement/service-agreement.md) once, before any paid work.

What you approve in a [proposal](../examples/proposal.md) is what we both agree to. Personal or health data needs the right agreement first, such as a Business Associate Agreement.

## Do you use AI?

Yes. It helps me research, polish my writing, review, and build faster, and I direct it. I make the decisions, approve every release, and answer for the result. [How I work with AI](../policies/ai-use.md) has the detail.

## What if something urgent comes up?

I work in planned appointments, and a care plan sets my response times in writing. An outage or incident in progress needs a provider with emergency coverage first. I take it from there, with the cause, the fix, and what to change.

For anything your business can't go a day without, someone on your side runs it day to day.

## How is the cost worked out?

After we talk, I send a short proposal: one recommendation, or options when there's a real choice, each with what it covers, its upkeep, and an estimate. Discovery sets the estimate. Unforeseen work or purchases are agreed with you before I add them.

Every option has the same security baseline, and a smaller option does less, not worse. The proposal also gives the schedule, and larger projects split into phases, each with its own scope and price, approved before it starts. How a price is set, invoices, and payment methods are in [pricing](../engagement/pricing.md).

## Do you run security training?

Yes, informational awareness sessions for groups, from parents and teachers to engineers and executives. They're not certified training. For controls, evidence, and audit preparation, see [security readiness](../guides/use-case-security-readiness.md).

## What if a project needs a specialist?

When a project needs a licensed installer, an independent auditor, or a penetration tester, I bring in a vetted one and write their role into the proposal.

I cover workflow automation, cloud and AI engineering, networks, devices, and connected systems, and security readiness. I get you ready for a review, and the reviewer makes the call. I work with your lawyer, accountant, or auditor on the technical side, and I take on personal or health data once the right agreements and insurance are in place. What I publish is general information, and a professional decides what applies to you.

# 1NEON guide: overview, names, and addresses

What 1NEON is, how its frame works, every kind of ID and name it shows, and the address of every page.

1NEON is neon1's client portal at neon1.tech/1NEON, where each client organization runs its projects with neon1. Every project moves through four layers, N E O N: **Needs** (what's wanted, and the options), **Execute** (the work), **Observe** (results checked against the goals), and **Normalize** (handover, training, and care).

## Who's who

- **neon1** is the *operator*. It proposes options, does the work, and can enter every client organization. The role comes from sign-in configuration, never from portal data.
- **A client organization** is one business or household neon1 works with. Its admins or neon1 invite its people.
- **neon1's own organization** has the slug `neon1` and the client ID **N1-0001**. There neon1 is also the client, so its people may approve options and name decision makers, which they can't do anywhere else.
- **A member** is a person in an organization with one access level there: viewer, editor, or admin. One person can belong to several organizations at different levels.

## IDs people see

| Looks like | What it is |
|---|---|
| `N1-0001`, `N1-0002` | A **client ID**, numbered in the order clients joined |
| `acme-dental` | An organization's **slug**, its handle in addresses (`/1NEON/o/acme-dental/...`) |
| `FLOW-1`, `MIG-2`, `HOME-1`, `PRJ-3` | A **project key**: a prefix from the project's template (`PRJ` Blank, `APP` Custom software, `MIG` Cloud migration, `MOD` Modernization, `FLOW` Workflow automation, `NET` Networks, `AI` AI assistant, `SEC` Security readiness, `HOME` Personal or home tech) and a number counted per organization and prefix, so `MIG-1` in two organizations are two projects |
| `0039`, `0039-r2` | A **proposal number** and one of its **revisions**. Each project has one proposal, and each change is issued as the next revision |
| `0039-r2-B` | An **option ID**: the revision and the option's letter. A decision names the ID it approved |
| `INV-0039-01` | An **invoice number**: the proposal's number (or the project key) and the invoice's place in the project. Card statements show `NEON1* INV003901` |

Items are shown by title. Their IDs only appear in links (`#item-…`).

## The frame around every signed-in page

- **Menu** (top left, **Menu** at the bottom on phones) opens every page. Choosing **Mini** on the profile also keeps a slim column of icons.
- **Organization chooser** at the top of the menu switches organizations. neon1 also sees **All clients**, read only ("Open a client to make changes").
- **Search** (the button, Ctrl K or ⌘K, or `/`) jumps to any page or project and starts common actions.
- **?** (top right) opens help for the page in view, with **Tour this page** (a spotlight tour, where the page has one) and **Full tour**.
- **The bell** glows when something new happened in the organization and lists what changed and who did it.
- **Neo** sits at the bottom right. It answers questions, links to pages, runs tours, and with the person's go-ahead does things for them.

Themes: Sentinel (**Providence** light, the default, and **Desert of the real** dark) and Matrix (**Awake** light and **Plugged** dark). **Match my device** follows the device setting.

## Addresses

Signed-in pages live under `https://neon1.tech/1NEON/`. `{org}` is the organization's slug and `{KEY}` a project key.

| Page | Address |
|---|---|
| Sign-in | `/1NEON/` |
| Home | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace` |
| Board | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow` |
| Projects (list and timeline), New project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects`, `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new` |
| A project, Overview | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}` |
| A project's layer | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, or `/normalize` |
| Options, files asked for, invoices, one item | `.../{KEY}/needs#options`, `.../needs#files`, `.../execute#billing`, `.../{layer}#item-{itemId}` |
| Proposal, one invoice | `.../{KEY}/proposal`, `.../{KEY}/invoices/{invoiceId}` |
| The service agreement, to sign | `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` |
| One layer across all projects | `/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/needs` (also `execute`, `observe`, `normalize`) |
| People, Files, Settings | `/1NEON/o/{org}/people`, `/documents`, `/settings` |
| Home's charts | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace#insights` |
| Your profile | `/1NEON/me` (two-step verification at `/1NEON/me#security`) |
| All clients (neon1 only) | `/1NEON/all/workflow` |
| FAQs, public | `/1NEON/faqs` |
| Guided walkthrough, public | `/1NEON/live` (whole story: `?play=full`. Short ones: `?play=free`, `invite`, `passkey`, `authenticator`, `texts`, `calendar`. One chapter: `?play=signin`, `profile`, `team`, `start`, `needs`, `listen`, `propose`, `decide`, `pay`, `build`, `change`, `observe`, `handover`, `final`, `care`, client: `&scenario=harborline`, `quillwork`, or `fenwick`) |
| Sample project, public | `/1NEON/example` (`?scenario=harborline`, `quillwork`, or `fenwick`) |
| Interactive demo, public | `/1NEON/demo/` |
| Privacy, terms, cookies, service agreement | `/1NEON/privacy`, `/1NEON/terms`, `/1NEON/cookies`, `/1NEON/agreement` |

Older links that say `execution` or `next` still work.

## Spotlight anchors

Tours point at named spots, which exist only on the page listed and only while on screen.

- **Every page:** `nav-home`, `nav-board`, `nav-projects`, `nav-layers`, `nav-files`, `nav-me` (menu entries, with the menu open or Mini on), `menu`, `search`, `help`.
- **Organization pages:** `notifications` (the bell).
- **Home:** `next-step-ask` (only when Next step shows), `needs-you`, `coming-up` (the calendar), `glance`, `weekly` (Finished per week), `get-to-know`, `get-started`, `activity`.
- **Board, All clients:** `board-column`, `board-card`.
- **Projects:** `new-project`, `project-list`.
- **One project:** `next-step`, `readiness` (Overview, until a decision), `stage`, `layers`, and on Needs `proposal` (the proposal strip under Options).
- **New project:** `wizard`. **One layer across projects:** `layer-list`.
- **People:** `invite`, `people-list`. **Files:** `upload`.
- **Settings:** `stages`. **Profile:** `passkey`.
