# 1NEON guide: projects, stages, layers, and items

How a project moves through stages and the four layers, every kind of item and its states, Next step, health, the proposal and its revisions, signed approvals, fixed prices and estimates, hours, purchases, handover acceptance, invoices, and payments.

## A project

A project is one piece of work for one organization. It has a key (such as `FLOW-1`), a name, a summary, an outcome ("what will be true when it's done"), a target date, a stage, a health, the people on it, sensitive-data flags (PII, PHI, or payment data), and items in four layers. Every change records who and when. Every edit carries the version last seen, so two people can't silently overwrite each other. The later save is shown what changed and asked to choose.

An admin can **archive** a project (kept, read only, off the main lists, and **Restore from archive** brings it back) or move it to **Trash** by typing its key. A trashed project leaves every view but is kept, and erased only if the client asks.

## Stages and the board

An organization's workflow is a row of stages, each tied to one layer. The defaults:

| Stage | Layer | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | Needs | Fit call held |
| Listen | Needs | Discovery complete, baseline metrics recorded |
| Propose | Needs | Options published to the client |
| Decide | Needs | An option approved |
| Build | Execute | All milestone tasks done (limit: 3 projects at once) |
| Verify | Observe | Checks pass, after metrics recorded |
| Hand over | Normalize | Handover accepted |
| Care | Normalize | Ongoing care, or closed |
| Closed | Normalize | (the end) |

The **Board** shows each project as a card (key, name, health, time in stage) in its stage's column. Editors and admins drag cards, or use **Move to** on a phone. In **Settings**, admins rename, reorder, limit, and hide stages and edit "Done when", confirming it's them to save. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it.

Two stages keep their roles under any name or position. **Decide** is the gate: moving past it without an approved option asks for a recorded reason. **Closed** ends a project, and **Reopen** (or dragging it back) moves it to the stage before. Moving backward never asks for a reason, and moving never changes health.

**All clients** (neon1 only) is the same board across every organization, read only.

## The four layers and their items

A project page has tabs for **Overview** and each layer. The onion beside the name has a ring per layer, Needs in the center, each filling as work gets done.

| Kind | Layer | What it is | Statuses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request | Needs | What the client wants, built as a sentence of taps: what, what for, what happens today, how often, when | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Discovery question | Needs | A question for the people who do the work, answered in their words | same |
| System or account | Needs | A system, account, vendor, or data source the work touches. Never passwords | same |
| Requirement | Needs | What the result must do: must, should, or could | same |
| Option | Needs | One way to solve it, from neon1: cost, timeline, scores for cost, quality, and effort (1 to 5, more is better), and whether neon1 recommends it | Draft, Proposed, Declined, Approved |
| Decision | Needs | The permanent record of an approved option, with the approver's signature | a record |
| Constraint or assumption | Needs | What the work depends on or is limited by, printed in the proposal | same as requests |
| Proposal revision | Needs | One issued, frozen revision, such as 0039-r1, made only by **Issue the proposal** | a record |
| File needed | Needs | A file neon1 asked the client for | Done once sent |
| Task, Milestone | Execute | A piece of work someone can finish, or a point everyone can see, such as a launch | same as requests |
| Change request | Execute | A change to what was agreed, with its effect on cost and dates | same |
| Hours | Execute | Time neon1 worked on one day, in quarter hours, and what it went to. Only neon1 adds entries | a record |
| Purchase | Execute | Something to buy for the approved option, with who buys it and its receipt | Open, Bought, Installed (done), Returned |
| Invoice | Execute | A bill for work or purchases, numbered when issued | Draft, Issued, Paid, Void |
| Payment | Execute | Money received against one invoice | a record |
| Status update | Execute | One line on how it's going, with a health. Posting it sets the project's health | a record |
| Measure | Observe | A number that shows it worked: unit, baseline, target, which way is better, dated readings | Done at its target |
| Check, Incident | Observe | Something to test before calling it done, or something that broke and what fixed it | same as requests |
| Handover step, Runbook, Training, Care, Retro | Normalize | A step before it's the client's, written steps for a repeated job, who learns what, ongoing care, and what to do differently | same as requests |

An item's title opens its panel: status, owner, due date, details, and comments. Its box ticks it done. A choice between options counts as one, done once one is approved. Updates, decisions, revisions, invoices, payments, and files aren't counted.

Who may do what:

- Anyone who can read the project, viewers too, may add a **request** and comment. Editors and admins add, edit, tick off, and delete other items. Only neon1 writes, shares, and withdraws **options** and makes **proposal revisions**, **invoices**, and **payments**, and issued ones can't be edited or deleted. A client who wants another option comments or adds a request. An **approved option** and its **decision** can't be edited or deleted. To change course, the decision maker approves a different option.

## Options and the proposal

Options are compared on the Needs tab (`#options`), each with its cost (one-time and recurring apart, with a first-year total), timeline, three scores, and any Recommended mark. An option can also carry neon1's hours, vendor costs, expected purchases, and the result the client can check.

An option's price is usually an **estimate**: a range of hours at an hourly rate that discovery sets. The client pays for hours worked, each listed under Hours, never past the high end without an approved change, and fewer hours cost less. Unforeseen work or purchases are agreed before they're added. A small, well-defined job may carry a **fixed** price instead: the whole price for the work described, changed only by an approved change. **How this adds up** lists the work line by line with hours, the expected total, and **When you pay**: the deposit at approval and the rest at handover.

A project has one proposal, issued in numbered revisions. While neon1 shapes the options it's a **draft** the client can read but not approve. **Issue the proposal** freezes and numbers a copy. The first 1NEON issued is 0039, so its first revision is **0039-r1**, and each option gets the revision plus a letter, such as **0039-r1-B**. A later change of option, estimate, or scope is issued as the next revision, 0039-r2. Earlier ones stay readable, marked "Replaced by a later revision".

**Read the proposal**, under the options (`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal`), shows discovery, goals, constraints and assumptions, every shared option with what's in and out, a cost table, and what each side will do. **Print or save as PDF** puts its ID and page number on every page. **Download Word** saves `neon1-{org}-proposal-0039-r1.docx`, and a marked-up copy uploaded to Files prompts "Is this a revision of Proposal 0039-r1?"

**Price checks.** Estimates are checked when a revision is issued and again after 30 days. Past that, approval waits until the decision maker chooses **Ask neon1 to refresh** and neon1 issues a revision with checked prices.

**Changes of scope.** A request added after approval asks "Does this change what was approved?" (**Yes, it changes it**, **No**, or **Not sure**). One marked as a change is flagged for, and answered in, the next revision.

## Approving and signing

**Approve this option** is offered only to the project's named **decision maker** (or several, any of whom may approve), or if nobody is named, an **admin of the client organization**. It's never offered to neon1, except in neon1's own organization (N1-0001), where neon1 is the client. Neo never approves for anyone. It points to **Approve this option**.

Approving needs all of these, and 1NEON says which is missing:

1. neon1 has issued the proposal, and the option is in the latest revision and unchanged since.
2. The revision is within its price check.
3. An admin of the client organization has signed neon1's [service agreement](../engagement/service-agreement.md) at an edition that still covers approvals. (Not needed in N1-0001.)

The approval screen restates what's accepted. The approver may add conditions ("only after 6pm"), then types their full name and ticks the consent box: "I agree to sign electronically. My typed name is my signature, and I can ask neon1 for a paper copy at any time."

The decision records the option ID, the approver's name and email, the time, its terms exactly as shown, and the signature (typed name, consent, a SHA-256 fingerprint of the signed terms, and the address and browser). If the option changed after it was opened, the approval is refused for review. It records that the organization agreed to that option's scope, cost, and timeline, as on paper.

Approving also adds the option's expected purchases to Execute, and drafts a deposit invoice for neon1 to check and issue when the price is in numbers: 30% of a fixed price or of an estimate's low end, unless the option states another share. Nothing reaches the client until it's issued.

Only a client admin, after confirming it's them, can name or change the decision maker, under People on the Overview.

### Changing the decision

Until the handover is accepted, the decision maker can choose a different option with **Choose this instead**. The screen says **Change to 0039-r1-C?** and shows what it replaces, what was already invoiced, the hours already logged, and the deposit asked now. A reason is required, and the change is signed like an approval.

- Nothing is billed twice. Money invoiced for the replaced decision counts toward the new one, so its deposit asks only for the difference, or nothing. An unissued deposit draft for the replaced decision is removed.
- Hours already logged count toward the new option's hours, and its high end still caps the total.
- If what was invoiced comes to more than the new option can cost, accepting the handover drafts a credit for the difference.
- The replaced decision stays in Needs, marked "replaced by a later decision", and the new one shows **Why it changed**. Everyone following Decisions and options is told.
- Going back to a replaced option waits until neon1 confirms it in the next revision with checked prices, then it shows **Go back to this option**.
- Once the handover is accepted, the decision stays.

## The service agreement

neon1's [service agreement](../engagement/service-agreement.md) covers every project with an organization, and anyone can read it at `/1NEON/agreement`. A client admin signs it once at `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` (from **Settings** or the notice under the options) with a typed name and the consent box, before the first approval. As they sign, they give the organization's legal name and mailing address, confirm they're authorized to sign for it, and choose about anonymized case studies (yes, decide later, no) and neon1's client list (ask first, yes, no). Nothing is selected for them. An admin can change either choice on the same page. The signature records the edition, a SHA-256 fingerprint of its text, the time, and where it came from, and the signed text can be downloaded. Edition 2.4 is signed before the next approval. Approvals made under 2.1 or 2.3 keep those terms, and those organizations' case-study choice stays at decide later until an admin chooses.

## Purchases, hours, and handover

Accepting a handover can carry a few words about the work. neon1 quotes them, without names, only if the client ticks the box.

**Purchases**, in Execute, start from the approved option's expected purchases. Each shows its estimate, the actual cost and where, who buys it, and its receipt. A bought item without a receipt is flagged.

- **The client buys it,** in the organization's name, and attaches the receipt (**Attach the receipt**).
- **neon1 buys it** only after the decision maker initials that neon1 buys it and is paid back at cost, in the signed approval or later on the purchase. Until then it says "Waiting on the decision maker's initials before neon1 buys it." neon1 attaches the receipt and bills exactly that amount, with no markup.

**Hours** (Execute, `#hours`) are logged by neon1 with date, quarter hours, and what they went to, and the client reads them only. On an estimate, the section shows hours against the range and a bar to the high end. Hours past the high end are listed, not billed. On a fixed price, hours are a record, not a bill. Issuing an invoice marks the hours it bills ("billed on INV-0039-02"), and a mistake is corrected with a credit.

**Handover acceptance.** Handover steps in Normalize are ticked as they're done, by either side. When all are, the decision maker sees "Every step is done" and chooses **Accept the handover**, with an optional note ("What you checked") and **Sign and accept the handover**, signed like an approval. One signature accepts every remaining step, each keeping its own record. **Check it and accept** accepts a single step early. An accepted step can't be unticked.

**Handover, review, and acceptance are separate records.** When the work is delivered, neon1 chooses **Record handover** with what was handed over. That date starts the 30-day defect period and asks the decision maker to review within 10 business days, by email and on the project. It also drafts the final invoice. Acceptance comes only from the client's signature, never from silence, and a review still open doesn't hold up payment for work properly performed.

**Waiting on the client.** When neon1 can't continue without the client's access, information, or decision, neon1 records what's needed with **Waiting on you**, and the client is told by email. The project shows when the work may pause (10 business days later) and when the project may end (30 calendar days later). A pause, for that or for an undisputed amount more than 7 days overdue, and an ending, are each recorded with a reason and told to the client. A pause never touches the client's own systems or data.

## Invoices and paying

Invoices are in Execute (`#billing`). neon1 makes them, and the client sees them only once issued.

| Type | When |
|---|---|
| Deposit | Drafted at approval: 30% of a fixed price or of an estimate's low end, unless the option states another share |
| Progress | Added by neon1 for a stage. On an estimate: the hours worked so far, less earlier invoices |
| Final | Drafted when neon1 records the handover: what's left on a fixed price, or the hours worked (never past the high end) less earlier invoices |
| Purchases at cost | Reimbursement for what neon1 bought, from the receipts |
| Care plan | The monthly fee for ongoing care |
| Credit | Reduces an issued invoice it names |

**Issue** numbers an invoice (**INV-0039-01**: the proposal's number, or the project key, and its place in the project), sets a due date (15 days by default), addresses it to the decision maker or a client admin, fixes its contents with a SHA-256 fingerprint, and tells the client by bell and email. Each invoice has its own page (`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{id}`) with lines, sales tax, total, credits, payments, balance due, terms, and how to pay, ready to print or save as a PDF. If the work comes to less than a deposit paid, neon1 refunds the difference as a credit.

An invoice reads as **Draft**, **Open**, **Partly paid**, **Overdue** (past due with an undisputed balance), **Paid in full**, **Void**, or **Credit**. The business day after an invoice is due, its billing contacts get a reminder.

**Disputing an invoice.** The decision maker or a client admin chooses **Dispute part of this invoice**, with the amount and why. neon1 sees it at once and answers on the invoice, with a credit, a corrected invoice, or an explanation, and marks it resolved. The undisputed amount stays due on the original date.

- **Online:** **See and pay**, then **Pay**, opens Stripe Checkout, bank transfer (ACH) first and card too. 1NEON never sees card or bank details. A card payment shows as paid at once. A bank payment shows as **bank payment clearing** until the bank clears it in a few business days. Meanwhile **Pay** is gone and nothing counts it overdue, so nobody pays twice. If the bank refuses it, no money moved, and the invoice reopens with the failed payment listed and **Pay again**. Billing contacts are told when a bank payment starts, clears, or fails.
- **By check, Zelle, or wire:** neon1 records it with **Record a payment** on arrival: amount, how it arrived, date, and a check number or confirmation.
- No surcharge for any way of paying.

Issued invoices and payments are permanent. A mistake is fixed with a **credit** or by voiding with a reason (**Void invoice**), both kept on record. An invoice with payments, or one clearing, is credited rather than voided. One whose only payment failed can be voided. Every signature, issued invoice, and payment is also kept write-protected for seven years.

## Next step

**Next step**, at the top of every project, shows the one thing to do now and who it waits on. The first that applies wins:

1. Client members: an invoice to pay ("Invoice INV-0039-01 is ready", **overdue**, or "didn't go through"), with **See and pay**. An invoice covered by a clearing bank payment isn't listed.
2. neon1: invoice drafts to check (**Check invoices**), then shared options not yet in an issued revision (**Issue the proposal** or **Issue r2**).
3. Options are shared: the approver sees "Choose an option" with **Compare options** (or that estimates are due a price check, or neon1 is preparing the proposal). Everyone else sees "Waiting on {decision maker} to choose an option", with **See options**.
4. Client members: "Send {n} files", with **Upload**.
5. The approver, once every handover step is done: **Review and accept**.
6. Anyone with open items assigned: "You have {n} open items here".
7. After an option is approved at or before Decide: "Next, move the project to {next stage}" (**Move to** for neon1, and clients read that neon1 moves it).
8. neon1 near Decide: "Add options" when none exist, "Share an option" when none is shared.
9. Otherwise the stage's goal. neon1 reads "To finish {stage}: {done when}" with **Move to {next stage}** (not past Decide without an approval). A client reads who has the work, what it's done when, and that nothing needs them now.

If nothing applies, it says "Nothing needs doing right now." In neon1's own organization, editors get the move as neon1 does.

## Health

Health is **Not assessed** (the start), **On track**, **At risk**, or **Off track**. Only people change it, on the Overview or by posting a status update ("How is it going?").

## Starting a project

**New project** (editors and admins) asks for a template, a name, what it is, what will be true when it's done, one real example of today's work, a target date, any sensitive data, and optional measures with baseline and target.

Templates start a project with fitting items: Blank (`PRJ`), Custom software (`APP`), Cloud migration (`MIG`), Modernization (`MOD`), Workflow automation (`FLOW`), Networks, devices, and connected systems (`NET`), AI assistant (`AI`), Security readiness (`SEC`), and Personal or home tech (`HOME`). Each starts with discovery questions, the systems involved, one requirement, one or two measures, and a check. Every template except Blank and Personal or home tech also starts with a handover checklist: accounts in the client's name, admin access transferred, docs delivered and walked through, users trained, older tools retired or merged, and neon1's access reduced or removed.

## The Overview tab

Overview shows any decision, the summary and outcome, measures with progress, a side column (health, stage and dates, the latest update, sensitive-data flags, people, **Archive this project**), and **How is it going?**. **People on this project** have roles: lead engineer, sponsor, decision maker, tech contact, stakeholder, and observer. Roles describe work and never grant access, except that a decision maker may approve.

### Ready for Execute

Until a decision exists, Overview shows **Ready for Execute**: a percent, a bar, and four steps. Everything in it is optional.

| Step | Counts for |
|---|---|
| **Outline** | 10 for each of six parts, up to 60 |
| **Assessment** | 10, once the project was sent for assessment from Home's Next step, or an option has been proposed |
| **Options** | 10, once an option is proposed or approved |
| **Decision** | 20, once an option is approved or a decision exists |

It reaches 100% only with a decision (at most 99% before), and then the card goes away. The six outline parts are what it is (the summary), how it works today (the real-example question), what done looks like (the outcome), who and what it touches (another answered discovery question, or a named system), how we'll know it worked (a measure with a baseline), and timing and limits (a target date, a constraint, or a requirement). [What to write](../guides/free-accounts.md#what-to-write) has what counts, a tip for each, and where each goes once work starts.

A part counts with about a dozen characters or more of real words. A starter question with no answer, or a starter item from a template, never counts alone. A project is **outlined** with the first three parts and **fully outlined** with all six. Each missing part links to where to write it, except for viewers. The same percent and parts show on Home's Next step and are what neon1 reads when it assesses a project.

docs.title: 1NEON guide: every page, what it shows, and who can do what
docs.text:
# 1NEON guide: every page, what it shows, and who can do what

Each signed-in 1NEON page: what it's for, what's on it, its states, and the actions on it with the access each one needs.

Access levels build up. **Viewers** read, comment, add requests, and approve when they're a project's decision maker. **Editors** also add and change work. **Admins** also invite people, change access and settings, and delete projects, files, and others' comments, after a recent "confirm it's you". neon1 acts as an admin everywhere but never approves for a client.

## Home

`/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace`.

Home is a grid of cards. **View** shows or hides each one, grouped as **To do**, **Movement**, **Visuals**, and **Shortcuts**, with each card's urgent, suggested, and to-know counts. Every organization offers the same cards; only setup and suggestion cards come and go. **Arrange** moves and resizes them, **Tidy up** repacks them, and the layout follows the person to any device.

- **Visuals** holds the charts: **Projects at a glance**, **Projects by layer**, **Numbers**, **Finished per week** (eight weeks), and, once turned on in View, **Project health** and **Delivery** (open and overdue work, the on-time rate, days to a decision, measures at target). Hovering a number says how it's counted. The old Insights address, `/1NEON/o/{org}/insights`, opens Home at these charts.

- **Needs you** lists what's waiting on you, most pressing first, each with its action: **See and pay** (an invoice due, overdue, or whose bank payment failed, but not one clearing), **Compare options**, **Review and accept**, **Upload file**, or **Open**. neon1 sees invoice drafts with **Check it**. Empty, it says "You're all caught up".
- **Calendar** shows a month at a time: work due, milestones, targets, and the organization's events. Choose a day to see it. Editors add leave, closures, meetings, or care plan dates. Under it are **Past**, **Overdue**, **Upcoming**, and **Repeated**.
- **Get started** is a setup checklist that disappears once done: the tour, a first project (editors), inviting the team, and a second step for admin actions (admins).
- **Your account**, in a free account only, shows the date it's deleted if nothing changes, with **Keep it 30 more days** (once) and **Download a copy**.
- **Get to know 1NEON**, in the side column for everyone but neon1's own people, links to **A sample project**, **From sign-up to client** (**The guided walkthrough** for neon1's own clients), **Try the demo**, **FAQs**, and, in a free account, **How accounts work**. **Hide** puts it away, and the profile's Tutorial setting brings it back.
- **Next step**, above Needs you for editors and admins (not neon1's own people), is where a project goes from outlined to assessed. A free account always sees it. A client organization sees it only while a project is waiting for an assessment: no options yet, and in the first stage.
  - With no projects, it says to outline one (up to three) with **Start a project**.
  - A free account lists each project with a six-segment meter of outline parts written, a tip for what's missing, and **Continue**. A fully outlined project says "Fully outlined" with **Review**. A client organization sees only what was sent and when.
  - Under the list, a required note of at least 20 characters and a checkbox for each project, up to three. **Request assessment** opens a last look at the projects, the note, and what each could still say. **Submit request** (or **Submit request anyway**) locks the box. **Keep editing** goes back.
  - A saved request goes to neon1 30 minutes after its last change, and never within an hour of the previous email. Until then **Edit** unlocks it and **Withdraw** stops it. After it goes, the card says "Sent" with the date, and an edit sends neon1 "Assessment request updated". The reply comes by email.
  - In a free account, **Book a 30-minute call** opens the booking page, or **ask me to email you** sends a call request with an optional note, once a week. A client organization sees **Contact neon1**. Neither the call nor the assessment needs the other first.

How the assessment and outline work is in [how 1NEON accounts work](../guides/free-accounts.md#what-to-write).

## Board, projects, and layers

| Page | Address | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Board | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow` | Every project as a card in its stage, with "Done when", the count, and any limit |
| Projects | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects` | A **List** (stage, health, target date, filtered by layer, sorted by stage, target date, or recent changes) or a **Timeline** (each project from start to target, colored by layer). **New project** (editors and admins) |
| New project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new` | A template, name, description, outcome, one real example, and optionally a target date, sensitive-data flags, and measures |
| One layer | `/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/{needs\|execute\|observe\|normalize}` | One layer's items across every project. Open a project to change them |
| All clients | `/1NEON/all/workflow` | neon1 only. Every client's projects on one read-only board, **By organization** or **One board** |

## One project

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}`, with tabs Overview, Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize (`/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, `/normalize`). The header shows the key, stage and time in it, name, health, and the onion, under **Next step**. Until a decision is made, the Overview shows **Ready for Execute** (see the projects guide). Files asked for show under Needs with **Upload**, and measures take dated readings.

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| Read, comment on items, add a request | Everyone in the organization |
| Add, edit, tick off, or delete other items. Edit name, summary, outcome, target date. Set health, post a status update, move stage, archive. Change people (not the decision maker) | Editors and admins |
| Name or change the decision maker | Client admins, after confirming it's them (in N1-0001 also neon1) |
| Approve an option, with a typed signature, ask neon1 to refresh a revision past its price check, initial a purchase neon1 buys, check and accept a handover step | The named decision maker, or with none named, a client admin. Approving only from an issued revision, within its price check, once the service agreement is signed |
| Add, share, or withdraw options, issue the proposal or its next revision. Draft, issue, void, or credit an invoice, record a check, Zelle, or wire payment | neon1 only |
| Add a purchase, attach a receipt, mark it bought, installed, or returned | Editors and admins (neon1 marks its own purchases bought only after the decision maker's initials) |
| Read issued invoices, pay one online | Everyone in the client organization |
| Move to Trash | Admins, after confirming it's them, typing the project's key |

## The proposal, an invoice, and the agreement

- **The proposal** (`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal`) is on neon1's letterhead for everyone in the organization: the latest revision (or the draft before the first), earlier ones marked replaced, and any signed approval. **Print or save as PDF** and **Download Word** keep a copy.
- **An invoice** (`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{id}`) is on neon1's letterhead, ready to print or save as a PDF. **Back to invoices** returns to the project.
- **The service agreement** (`/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` signed in, `/1NEON/agreement` public) shows its edition and **Signatures**: who signed which edition and when. A client admin signs it once, choosing about anonymous case studies and neon1's client list, and can change either later on the same page.
- **All clients** also has **Potentials** (`/1NEON/all/prospects`, neon1 only): free accounts that aren't clients yet.

## People, files, and settings

- **People** (`/1NEON/o/{org}/people`) shows who's in the organization, with title, access, and status (**Invited**, **Joined**, **Deactivated**). Admins **Invite people** (up to 50 emails at once, with an access level and optional names and titles), see whether each invitation went out (queued, sent, or failed), **Resend** (rate limited), change access or titles, or **deactivate** someone until reactivated. neon1's own access shows without a way to change it.
- **Files** (`/1NEON/o/{org}/documents`) lists every file. Anyone, viewers too, can **Upload** at Organization level, under a project, or in one of its layers, up to 100 MB each (a free account holds 10 files, 10 MB each and 50 MB in all). **Move** refiles one, and issued proposals are listed too. Files move through **Receiving**, **Checking** (virus and size), **Ready**, **Rejected** (a threat found), or **Failed**. PDFs, pictures, and text open in a tab, and others download. Uploaders and admins can delete.
- **Settings** (`/1NEON/o/{org}/settings`) has **Where**: the organization's website and where it's based, checked as on sign-up. Any admin can **Change** it without confirming. It's optional. It also shows the agreement's signer and edition (or "not signed yet") with **Read and sign**, the case study and client list choices, **Download everything** under Your data, **Report a bug**, and the board's stages: name, layer, "Done when", optional limit, **Show** or **Hide**, and order. **Save workflow** saves all (admins, after confirming it's them). A stage holding projects can't be removed.
- **Your profile** (`/1NEON/me`) has name, title, phone (only you see it), time zone, motion, menu (Default or Mini), and **Notifications** by group (email, text, or neither). Most changes save by themselves. Also here: texts, **Two-step verification** at `#security`, **Replay the tutorial**, and **Sign out** (also beside your name in the open menu, in two taps). Two-step changes and signing out take effect at once.
- **Contact** (`/1NEON/contact`), in the menu for every account, has email hello@neon1.tech, call or text (424) 32-neon1, and a booked call, with the hours I answer. Anything about a project is best written in that project.

## Public pages

The sign-in screen (`/1NEON/`), FAQs, service agreement, sample project, guided walkthrough, interactive demo, and policies are open without signing in. Neo on the sign-in screen is the public Neo, which only knows neon1's public pages.

docs.text:
# 1NEON guide: sign-in, confirming it's you, notifications, and texts

How people get into 1NEON, why admin actions ask to confirm it's you, the three second steps, notifications, texts, and what to do when something is lost.

## Getting in

People join by invitation or by making their own free account. An admin of the organization, or neon1, invites a person by email, and they open the link and enter their email. When sign-up is open, someone new chooses **Create an account** on the sign-in screen and gives:

- An email, their name (one name is fine), which describes them best, and their organization's name (not asked of an individual, optional for **Something else**).
- Optionally, a website or public page, a city and state (a state alone, or a place outside the US), and how they found neon1.

Each field is checked as it's filled in. The email's domain must take mail and can't be a temporary mailbox, a website must look like a web address (it's never visited), and a US city is spelled properly when it's on the public places list and kept as typed when it isn't.

Either way, people sign in with an 8-digit code sent to their email (valid a few minutes, in the browser that asked), or with a passkey once added. There are no passwords. The first sign-in offers a one-minute welcome tour.

A free account holds up to 3 projects, 50 items in a project, and 10 files (10 MB each, 50 MB in all), with no inviting, approvals, proposals, billing, or Neo until neon1 converts it to a client account. A client account takes any file up to 100 MB. How a free account works, including the assessment, the call, the outline tips, and its 30-day deletion with check-ins at 7 and 14 days and a final notice at 21, is in [free 1NEON accounts](../guides/free-accounts.md). **Keep it 30 more days** (once) and **Download a copy** are on Home's **Your account**.

An email address can't be changed on the profile. An admin invites the new address and deactivates the old one.

## Confirming it's you

Admin actions need a recent second-step confirmation, so a stolen email account isn't enough: inviting people, changing access or deactivating someone, changing settings (stages), naming a decision maker, deleting a project, and deleting someone else's comment or file. 1NEON asks "Confirm it's you" and offers the person's second steps. Once confirmed, it doesn't ask again for 12 hours in that sign-in.

The second steps are added on the profile under **Two-step verification** (`/1NEON/me#security`):

- **Passkey:** face, fingerprint, or device PIN. Phishing-resistant, and offered first at sign-in once added.
- **Authenticator app:** **Set up**, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type its 6-digit code.
- **Text-message codes,** once a mobile number is verified for texts.

A second one is a backup. If one is lost, confirm with another, remove the lost one, and add a new one. If all are lost, email hello@neon1.tech from the account's address. There's no self-service reset, and email alone isn't enough, since a stolen mailbox is what the second step guards against. neon1 confirms who it is by calling a number already on record (never one from the email), plus another admin's written OK if the organization has one. Then the lost methods are removed and dated, and the person is emailed to add a new one. Email codes still sign you in meanwhile. Only admin actions wait.

## Notifications and texts

The bell glows when something new happens. Each person chooses per group on the profile whether it also reaches them by email, text, or neither:

| Group | What counts | Email by default |
